mcqs.q: A Class III lesion is located on the:
opts: Proximal surface of anterior teeth WITHOUT the incisal angle
mcqs.explain: Class III lesions are on the proximal surfaces of anterior teeth, without involvement of the incisal angle (that would be Class IV).

mcqs.q: Most Class III and IV lesions are restored with:
mcqs.explain: Almost all Class III/IV restorations are appropriately restored with composite for esthetics.

mcqs.q: An effective composite bond in a Class III preparation requires:
mcqs.explain: The operating area must be adequately isolated (rubber dam) to achieve an effective bond.

mcqs.q: A contraindication to composite in Class III/IV is:
opts: An area that cannot be adequately isolated
mcqs.explain: Composite is contraindicated when the field cannot be isolated, and where the restoration extends onto the root surface.

mcqs.q: When a Class III restoration extends onto the root surface (no marginal enamel), polymerization shrinkage tends to create a:
mcqs.explain: With no marginal enamel at the root, polymerization shrinkage of the composite forms a V-shaped contraction gap between root and composite.

mcqs.q: To reduce microleakage/gap on a root-surface margin, you can place a:
mcqs.explain: An RMGI liner on the root portion reduces microleakage, gap formation and recurrent caries.

mcqs.q: Tooth preparation for a Class III composite should be:
opts: Always extended to the incisal angle
mcqs.explain: Composite preparations should be as conservative as possible; the extent is determined by the size, shape and location of the defect.

mcqs.q: The extent of a Class III preparation is determined by the:
opts: Size, shape and location of the defect
mcqs.explain: Unlike amalgam, the composite preparation outline is dictated by the size, shape and location of the carious defect.

mcqs.q: The FIRST step in a Class III/IV composite procedure is:
mcqs.explain: Shade selection is done first (before the tooth dehydrates and lightens), so the chosen shade is accurate.

mcqs.q: Pre-operative assessment of occlusion is especially important in:
mcqs.explain: Occlusion is particularly assessed in Class IV (incisal-angle) restorations, which bear occlusal/incisal loads.

mcqs.q: Composite restorations are primarily retained by:
opts: A micromechanical bond from acid etching and resin bonding
mcqs.explain: Composite is retained by the micromechanical bond produced by acid-etching and resin bonding, not mechanical undercuts.

mcqs.q: When there is a choice, the preferred entry for a proximal anterior lesion is:
mcqs.explain: The lingual/palatal approach is preferable because it conserves the facial enamel and esthetics.

mcqs.q: An ADVANTAGE of the lingual approach is that:
opts: Facial enamel is conserved for enhanced esthetics
mcqs.explain: Lingual access conserves facial enamel, colour-matching is less critical, and any discoloration over time is less visible.

mcqs.q: A reason colour-matching is LESS critical with a lingual approach is that:
opts: The intact facial enamel masks the restoration
The lingual surface is invisible to the patient only
mcqs.explain: Because the facial enamel is preserved and shows through, the lingual composite is less visible, so exact colour matching is less critical.

mcqs.q: An indication for the FACIAL approach is:
opts: The carious lesion is positioned facially
mcqs.explain: Facial entry is indicated when the lesion is positioned facially, when teeth are irregularly aligned (poor lingual access), or when caries is extensive.

mcqs.q: Irregularly aligned anterior teeth may force a facial approach because:
mcqs.explain: When teeth are crowded/irregular, lingual access can be impossible, so the facial approach is used despite its esthetic cost.

mcqs.q: A bevel or rounded cavosurface on the enamel margin is used to:
opts: Increase the bonding surface area and improve the margin
mcqs.explain: A bevel/rounded cavosurface increases the etched enamel surface area for bonding and improves marginal blending.

mcqs.q: Which sequence is correct for a bonded Class III composite?
opts: Prepare → (liner) → etch → bond → place & cure composite → finish/polish
mcqs.explain: After preparation (and a liner if needed), the enamel/dentin is etched, bonding agent applied, composite placed and cured, then finished and polished.

mcqs.q: This finished anterior restoration is a:
mcqs.explain: The image shows a finished Class III composite restoration on the proximal surface of an anterior tooth.

mcqs.q: Local anaesthesia and rubber-dam isolation in Class III are performed:
opts: As part of pre-operative preparation, before cutting
mcqs.explain: Pre-operative steps include shade selection, occlusal assessment, local anaesthesia and rubber-dam isolation before preparation.

mcqs.q: The incisal angle is involved in which class (NOT Class III)?
mcqs.explain: Class IV involves the proximal surface AND the incisal angle of anterior teeth; Class III spares the incisal angle.

mcqs.q: The discoloration of a lingual-approach restoration over the years is:
mcqs.explain: Because the restoration is approached lingually, any later discoloration/deterioration is less visible from the facial aspect.

saqs.a: A lesion on the proximal surface of an anterior tooth WITHOUT involving the incisal angle.

saqs.q: List the contraindications to composite in Class III/IV.
saqs.a: An area that cannot be isolated with rubber dam, and a restoration that extends onto the root surface (contraction gap).

saqs.q: What is the first step, and how is composite retained?
saqs.a: Shade selection is the first step; composite is retained by a micromechanical bond (acid etch + resin bonding).

saqs.q: Why is the lingual/palatal approach preferred?
saqs.a: It conserves facial enamel (esthetics), colour-matching is less critical, and discoloration is less visible.

saqs.q: Give two indications for the facial approach.
saqs.a: Lesion positioned facially, and irregularly aligned teeth (poor lingual access); also extensive caries.

saqs.q: Why does a root-surface margin form a contraction gap, and how is it managed?
saqs.a: No marginal enamel + polymerization shrinkage → V-shaped gap; manage with an RMGI liner on the root portion.

saqs.q: What is the purpose of bevelling the enamel margin?
saqs.a: To increase the bonding surface area (more etched enamel) and improve marginal blending.
